title: Starfish, Sandbars & Sunburned Smiles: A Family Day on Saona Island
caption: Two parents, three kids from Ohio and one very long, very perfect Caribbean day — what a Saona trip really looks like when you're traveling as a family.
prelude: If your family vacation has exactly one 'big day out,' make it this one. Saona is the trip the kids will still be talking about at Thanksgiving.
post:
## The early start (yes, it's worth it)
Pickup comes early, so pack the night before: reef-safe sunscreen, a change of clothes for each kid, a dry bag for phones and a few small bills for tips. The air-conditioned ride gives everyone one last nap before the fun starts.

## Speedboat out, catamaran back
The crossing is where your kids decide this is the best day ever. The speedboat skims the coast fast enough to make everyone squeal, and the crew are pros at handing out life vests in the right sizes. On the way home, the catamaran is the opposite: music, shade, a breeze and plenty of room for little ones to sprawl out.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## The Natural Pool: standing in the middle of the ocean
This is the moment. The boat stops on a sandbar inside Cotubanamá National Park, and suddenly the whole family is standing waist-deep in clear water, far from shore, with giant red starfish on the sand. The guides show the kids how to look without lifting them out of the water — a great little lesson in respecting wildlife.

## Lunch and lazy hours at Abanico Beach
On Saona you get about three hours, two of them on the beach: palm shade, soft white sand and a buffet with grilled chicken, fresh fish and Dominican sides that even picky eaters can work with. The reserved loungers mean you're not hunting for a spot while juggling towels and a toddler.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Family tips we'd give our friends
- **Ages:** great from about 4 up; babies are welcome, but a long day is a long day.
- **Bring:** rash guards (the sun is strong on the water), water shoes for the sandbar, snacks for the bus.
- **Budget:** the price includes transport, boats, food and drinks — the only extras are photos and souvenirs.
- **Pace:** let the kids nap on the catamaran home; you'll get an hour of peace with a cold drink.

## Is it right for your crew?
If you want one day that feels like a postcard and keeps everyone from toddlers to grandparents happy, Saona is it. Book a few days ahead in high season — and message us on WhatsApp with your kids' ages, so we can bring the right vests.

title: Our Honeymoon Splurge: Lobster, Loungers and a Private Corner of Saona
tour: Saona Island Exclusive: The Lobster Feast
caption: We said 'I do' in Nashville and 'yes, the VIP one' in Punta Cana. Here's why the lobster-feast version of Saona was worth every extra dollar.
prelude: Honeymoons are for the upgrade you'd never buy on a normal trip. For us, it was a front-row lounger on Abanico Beach and a full pound of grilled lobster.
post:
## Why we chose the Exclusive
We knew we wanted to see Saona — everybody told us to. But we also knew we didn't want a crowded beach day. The Exclusive package takes the classic trip and adds the things couples actually care about: door-to-door transfers, a reserved VIP area right on the sand, cold Presidente beers and a fresh grilled lobster each.

## Catamaran mornings
The day starts with a catamaran party: live music, an open bar and a crew that knows exactly when to turn the volume down so you can just sit at the bow and watch the water change color. We clinked plastic cups of rum punch at 10 a.m. and called it a honeymoon tradition.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## The Natural Pool, hand in hand
Halfway out, the boat stops on a sandbar in the middle of the sea. You climb down and stand in clear, waist-deep water with starfish around your feet. Our guide took the photo we'll put on every anniversary card from now on.

## Lobster on Abanico Beach
On the island we had about three hours, most of it on Abanico Beach in our own front-row loungers. Then lunch: a gourmet buffet with meats, fish and sides, and on top of it a full pound of grilled lobster, butter and lime on the side. Eat it slowly, with your toes in the sand. That's the whole tip.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Honeymoon notes
- **Tell us it's your honeymoon** when you book — the crew loves an excuse to celebrate.
- **Pack light:** swimsuit, cover-up, sunscreen, a dry bag, a little cash for photos.
- **Plan it mid-trip,** not on your last day; you'll want a lazy pool day after.
- **Dinner that night?** Keep it light. You'll still be full of lobster.

If you only splurge once in Punta Cana, splurge on this. Message us on WhatsApp with your dates and we'll save you two loungers in the front row.

title: Empty Nesters Underwater: Rediscovering Each Other on Catalina's Reefs
caption: The kids are in college, the house is quiet, and Karen and Mike from Ohio finally booked the snorkeling trip they'd been talking about for twenty years.
prelude: We spent two decades planning vacations around soccer schedules. This time we planned one around coral reefs — and floated face-down together for an hour, grinning into our masks.
post:
## A different kind of island day
Catalina is the island for people who want to be *in* the water, not just next to it. Instead of a party boat, this trip is built around the reefs that ring the island — and for two fifty-somethings who hadn't snorkeled since their honeymoon, it was a gentle, wonderful way back in.

## Getting there
Pickup at the hotel, a stop at a local artisan shop for souvenirs, then a scenic boat ride of about 25 minutes over to the island with drinks served on board. Long day (around 12 hours), but none of it feels rushed.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## The reef: a kaleidoscope just under the surface
The crew hands out masks, snorkels and buoyancy aids — which means you float effortlessly, even if you're not a strong swimmer. Then you put your face in the water and the world switches on: schools of blue tang, parrotfish nibbling coral, sergeant majors darting in stripes. Mike pointed at everything. Karen counted fish species out loud underwater (you can't, it just comes out as bubbles).

## Lunch on the sand
After the reef there's a beachfront buffet with drinks, and time on pristine white sand. We split a lounger, napped, swam again, and talked about the next trip — which is maybe the best sign of a good one.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Tips for first-time (or long-lapsed) snorkelers
- **The buoyancy aid is your friend.** Wear it; it takes all the effort out.
- **Defog trick:** a drop of baby shampoo or a little spit inside the mask works wonders.
- **Don't touch the coral** — it's alive and it scrapes.
- **Sun:** a long-sleeve rash guard protects your back while you float.

If you're an empty-nest couple looking for a day that feels like a gentle adventure, Catalina is it. Message us on WhatsApp and we'll tell you about the best days for calm water.

title: The Bachelorette Party Boat: Seven Girls, One Catamaran, Zero Regrets
tour: Bávaro Party Boat: Dance on the Waves
caption: Matching swimsuits, a bride-to-be sash and an open bar in the middle of the Caribbean. Here's how to plan the perfect Bávaro party-boat send-off.
prelude: Every bachelorette trip needs one moment the group chat will never stop talking about. Ours happened waist-deep in the ocean, cocktail in hand, with the bride leading a conga line.
post:
## Why a party boat is the move
Planning a bachelorette in Punta Cana means juggling seven schedules, seven budgets and one bride who 'doesn't want anything crazy' (she does). The Bávaro party boat checks every box in about four hours: transport, open bar, music, swimming and snorkeling — no planning required beyond matching outfits.

## Getting on board
An air-conditioned van picks you up at the hotel (pregame playlist recommended). Then it's onto a modern catamaran with a premium open bar and a crew whose job is basically to make sure your group has the best time on the water.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Dancing on the waves
The boat cruises along the Bávaro coast with the latest hits blasting. Our bride got pulled up for a dance-off (she won). The crew knows how to keep the energy high without it ever feeling sloppy.

## The Natural Pool: cocktails in the middle of the ocean
The boat anchors over a shallow sandbar and everybody jumps in. Standing waist-deep in turquoise water, drink in hand, music still playing from the boat — this is THE photo. There's also a guided snorkel session with gear included, for anyone who wants a breather from dancing.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Bachelorette planning tips
- **Book together, pay separately:** ask us and we'll help organize payments per person.
- **Tell us about the bride** — the crew loves a bride-to-be.
- **Bring** waterproof phone pouches, sunscreen, a cover-up and cash for tips.
- **Hydrate:** alternate rum punch with water; the Caribbean sun doesn't play.

Four hours, zero logistics, endless photos. Message us on WhatsApp with your date and group size — we'll take care of the rest.

title: Swinging Over the Caribbean: An Instagram Couple's Day on Montaña Redonda
caption: Jess and Marcus from Austin came to Punta Cana with a shot list. One hilltop above the northeast coast delivered every frame on it — and lunch.
prelude: We'd seen the photo a hundred times: a couple on a swing, nothing behind them but sky, lagoon and green hills. The real thing turned out to be even better, and our camera roll has the proof.
post:
## Why this hill is all over your feed
Montaña Redonda rises about 300 meters above the northeast coast of the Dominican Republic, and the summit gives you a full 360-degree view: the Atlantic on one side, two wide lagoons and patchwork farmland on the other, and the hills of the Cordillera Oriental fading into the haze. For a couple who plans vacations around photos, it's basically an open-air studio with the best backdrop on the island.

## The ride up is part of the content
Pickup is right at your hotel lobby, and the last stretch is where the fun starts: a Safari Truck grinds its way up the steep road to the top. It's open-air and bumpy, so hold on to your hat and your phone at the same time. Marcus filmed the whole climb one-handed. It's now our most-watched story of the year.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Swings, hammocks and the famous 'flying' broomsticks
At the summit, everything is set up for pictures. The swings face out over the slope, so in the shot it looks like you're sailing over the valley. The hammocks are made for a lazy, sun-soaked couple photo. And the broomsticks are the silly one: you sit, kick your legs up and, from the right angle, you're a witch flying over the Caribbean. Honest note: the camera angle does a lot of the work, which is exactly why the photos look so dramatic. There's dedicated free time for photography, so nobody hurries you along while you get the light right.

## Lunch with a view
Once the shoot is done, you sit down to a traditional Dominican lunch right at the summit, with the breeze coming up the hill and the lagoons spread out below. We won't spoil the menu, but it's real home-style cooking, and somehow it tastes better 300 meters up.

## Macao: a local shop and the beach
On the way back you stop at a local shop in Macao and then get time on Macao Beach: wide golden sand and Atlantic waves that are a lot livelier than the calm water back in Bávaro. Perfect for one last barefoot shot; just respect the surf if you go in.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Our shot-list tips
- **Wear color.** The background is green and blue, so red, yellow or white really pops.
- **Secure everything.** It can be breezy at the top: hair ties, a hat with a strap, a phone lanyard.
- **Sun protection first.** There's very little shade on a hilltop, so put on sunscreen before the photo session, not after.
- **Shoes:** sneakers or sturdy sandals for the truck and the summit; save the cute ones for the beach.
- **Swimsuit under your outfit** if you want a dip at Macao, plus a small towel.

## Is it worth it?
At $90 per person for 4–5 hours, with hotel transfers, the truck ascent, the swings and lunch included, it's one of the best-value photo days around Punta Cana — and it still leaves your afternoon free. Send us a WhatsApp with your dates and we'll help you pick a clear-sky day for your shoot.

title: Mud, Buggies and a Cave Swim: The Spring Break Day the Group Chat Won't Let Go
caption: Six friends from Penn State, one week of spring break and a fleet of off-road buggies that left us covered in more mud than any of us expected.
prelude: Every spring break crew has one guy who says, 'We should do something real.' This year he was right — and 'something real' involved a steering wheel, a muddy trail and a swim inside a cave.
post:
## Why buggies beat another pool day
By day three, the swim-up bar had lost a little of its magic. We wanted something that felt like an actual adventure without costing a fortune or eating our whole week. The Evolution Buggies tour hit every mark: hotel pickup, your own all-terrain buggy, a swim in a natural underground cave, a plantation visit and an afternoon at Macao Beach — for $50 a person. That's less than one night out.

## Gear up and get filthy
After pickup, the crew gets everyone sorted with buggies and safety gear and runs through the basics. Then you're off on rugged dirt trails through the Dominican countryside: past pastures, palm groves and small farms, splashing through every puddle the trail throws at you. And there are a lot of puddles. Within twenty minutes, Tyler looked like he'd been dipped in chocolate. The guides set the pace and the route — stick behind them, keep your distance from the buggy in front, and save the racing for video games.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## The Macao Cave cenote
Just when you're caked in dirt, the tour drops you into the coolest stop of the day: a hidden cenote inside a natural cave near Macao. You climb down out of the heat into clear, fresh water surrounded by rock, and swim in what feels like a secret pool. It's half adventure, half shower. Nobody wanted to get out.

## A plantation stop: cacao, coffee and tobacco
Next comes a traditional plantation, where you see how three of the country's signature crops are grown — cacao, coffee and tobacco. The Dominican Republic is one of the world's big cigar producers, so this was the stop where the guys who claimed to know about cigars got very quiet and started actually listening.

## Macao Beach to finish
The day ends with time to relax on Macao Beach, a wide sweep of golden sand with real Atlantic waves. Rinse off, lie down, and let the sun bake the last of the mud off your legs.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Tips from the crew
- **Wear clothes you're ready to retire.** The mud stains; don't bring your favorite white shirt.
- **Bring a bandana or buff** and sunglasses for dust and splashes.
- **Swimsuit under your clothes,** a towel, and a change of clothes in a plastic bag for the ride home.
- **Waterproof phone pouch or an action cam** — you'll want the footage.
- **Driving rules:** ask us about requirements for drivers and passengers before you book, so nobody is stuck in the passenger seat by surprise.
- **Save the beers for after.** You're driving.

## Book it
Fifty bucks a head for mud, a cave, a plantation and a beach is the best deal of the trip. Message us on WhatsApp with your group size and dates, and we'll line up the buggies.

title: Five Centuries in One Day: A Retired Couple Walks Santo Domingo's Colonial Zone
caption: Linda taught history for 34 years; Doug mostly wanted a good lunch. The First City tour gave both of these Ontario retirees exactly what they came for.
prelude: We'd done the beach. We'd done the buffet. What we hadn't done was stand beneath the oldest cathedral in the Americas — and that turned out to be the highlight of our winter escape.
post:
## Why trade a beach day for a 10-hour tour
Let's be honest up front: this is a long day. The tour runs about 10 hours, and a good part of that is the highway drive from the Punta Cana area to the capital and back. But the transportation is private and air-conditioned, entrance fees, a traditional lunch with drinks and full liability insurance are all included, and you don't have to plan a single thing. For two people who no longer enjoy driving in unfamiliar cities, that mattered.

## The Colonial Zone: where the story begins
Santo Domingo was founded in the 1490s by Bartholomew Columbus, Christopher's brother, which makes it the oldest European city still standing in the Americas. Its Colonial Zone is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and you feel why within minutes: cobblestone streets, coral-stone facades, wrought-iron balconies and shady plazas. Calle Las Damas, often called the first paved street in the New World, runs right through it. Linda kept stopping to read plaques. Doug kept stopping to find shade. Both are valid strategies.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Alcázar de Colón
The guided tour of the Alcázar takes you through the palace built in the early 1500s for Diego Columbus, Christopher's son, when he governed the colony. The thick walls, period furniture and views over the Ozama River make it easy to imagine viceregal life five hundred years ago.

## The First Cathedral of the Americas
Then comes the Cathedral, completed around 1540 and the first ever built in the New World. The guided visit explains its blend of Gothic and Renaissance styles and the history layered into its chapels. It's cool and quiet inside, a welcome pause in the city heat.

## Los Tres Ojos
Los Tres Ojos is a park of limestone caves holding clear, blue-green lagoons. It's a striking change of scene after the old town. Fair warning: there are steps down into the caves, uneven in places, so take your time and use the railings.

## Chocolate, amber and larimar
The day also includes the Chocolate Museum and visits to jewelry workshops. Larimar, the sky-blue stone, is found only in the Dominican Republic, and Dominican amber is famous for tiny ancient insects and leaves trapped inside. Shopping is entirely optional; we bought one larimar pendant and called it our anniversary present.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Notes for travelers of a certain age
- **Comfortable walking shoes:** the cobblestones are uneven, and you'll be on your feet a fair bit.
- **Knees a concern?** Tell us before booking so we can talk through the steps at Los Tres Ojos.
- **Cover shoulders and knees** for the Cathedral; a light scarf does the trick.
- **Hat, sunscreen and a water bottle:** the capital is hotter than the coast.
- **Bring a neck pillow** for the drive and a few small bills for tips.

## Should you go?
At $70 per person with entrance fees, guides, lunch and drinks included, it's the most meaningful day you can spend away from the beach. Message us on WhatsApp with your dates and any mobility questions, and we'll make it comfortable for you.

title: Horses, Cacao Pods and a River Swim: The Countryside Day Our Little Ones Loved
caption: We worried a full-day tour would be too much for a four- and a seven-year-old. Instead, the Cultural Safari became the day they now narrate to anyone who'll listen.
prelude: Little kids don't care about 'authentic culture.' They care about big trucks, horses and jumping into rivers. Luckily, the Cultural Safari has all three — and the culture sneaks in on its own.
post:
## Out past the resort walls
Our resort was lovely, but after five days the kids thought the whole Dominican Republic was a pool and a buffet. We wanted them to see real life here: farms, towns, a school. The Cultural Safari is built for exactly that, and it's described as suitable for all ages. Be ready for a full day, though: it runs about 8 hours, in open-air 4x4 safari trucks that are bumpy, breezy and sunny. Our two thought the truck alone was worth the trip.

## A visit to a local school
One of the first stops is a local school. Our seven-year-old went quiet, then started comparing everything to her own classroom in Toronto: the desks, the uniforms, the alphabet on the wall. It was the best conversation we had all vacation. Please ask before taking photos of children, and if you'd like to bring something for the school, message us first to ask what's actually useful.

## Coffee, cacao and tobacco
Next come mountain plantations, with educational tours of coffee, cacao and tobacco farms and tastings. The kids cracked a cacao pod and couldn't believe chocolate starts as a sticky white fruit. They stuck to the chocolate; we tried the coffee.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Higüey: the Basilica and the market
In Higüey you visit the Basilica of Our Lady of Altagracia, with its soaring arch that the kids called 'the giant hands.' It's one of the most important pilgrimage sites in the Caribbean, so dress respectfully. The local market next door is noisy, colorful and fascinating; keep small hands in yours.

## Ranch lunch, river swim and horses
At a family-run ranch, there's a traditional lunch from a buffet, plus an open bar. Then everybody swims in the Maimón River, which was the high point for our four-year-old. After that comes a scenic horseback ride along tropical trails. Tell us your children's ages when you book so we can talk through how it works for little riders.

## Macao Beach to wind down
The day ends with beach time at Macao Beach. Wide golden sand and Atlantic waves: let the kids dig, but keep them close at the water's edge.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Tips for parents of little ones
- **Swimsuits under clothes,** plus towels and a full change of clothes for each child.
- **Water shoes** for the river, sunscreen and hats with straps for the open truck.
- **Snacks and a refillable water bottle** — it's a long day for small bodies.
- **Cover shoulders and knees** for the Basilica; a light scarf works for adults.
- **Small bills** for the market and tips.

## Is it for your family?
At $90 per person, with transport, farm tours and tastings, lunch, the river, horses and the beach included, it's the most complete day out around Punta Cana. Send us a WhatsApp with your kids' ages and travel dates, and we'll help you plan it.

title: Captain and First Mate: Our Couple's Speedboat Day on the Bávaro Coast
caption: Jess and Ryan from Denver swapped the resort pool for the wheel of their own speedboat, then floated over a coral reef full of tropical fish.
prelude: There's a special kind of trust in handing your partner the controls of a speedboat. Ten minutes in, we were laughing too hard to argue about who drives better.
post:
## Why we picked the speedboat
We'd done the swim-up bar. We'd done the couples massage. By day four in Bávaro we wanted one outing that felt a little wild and belonged to just the two of us. This tour is built for exactly that: one private speedboat per couple. No strangers on the bench next to you, no waiting your turn, and nobody to judge your steering except the person you married.

## A pickup that fits your vacation
Hotel transfers run every hour, which sounds like a small detail until you're on vacation and the alarm clock is the enemy. We chose a slot after a slow breakfast, packed one bag between us and headed for the water without any rush. That flexibility alone made it feel less like an excursion and more like our own plan.

## Taking the wheel
The setup is simple and reassuring: an expert guide drives a lead boat, and the couples follow behind across the turquoise water. You get all the thrill of the throttle without having to figure out where the reef is. Ryan drove first, grinning like a sixteen-year-old with a brand-new license. Then it was my turn, and for the record, I was smoother on the turns. Spray on your sunglasses, the line of palm trees sliding past, the water shifting from deep blue to that unreal pale turquoise: it was the most awake we felt all week.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Face down over the coral
Then the engines go quiet. At a protected coral reef the guide hands out professional snorkeling gear, and the whole mood of the day flips. After all that noise and speed, it's suddenly just the sound of your own breathing and a world of color below you. Tropical fish drifted through the coral in little schools, flashes of blue and yellow stripes, a parrotfish working away at the reef. We kept tapping each other's shoulders and pointing, like kids at an aquarium.

## The Bávaro Natural Pool
The last stop is the Bávaro Natural Pool, a shallow, sandy stretch of sea where you can stand in clear, warm water a long way from the beach. No mask, no effort, just a refreshing dip with the boats bobbing nearby. If you're the kind of couple who takes a photo for the fridge, this is where you take it.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Tips for couples
- **Decide who drives first** before you leave the hotel. You can swap along the way.
- **Follow the lead boat** and the guide's signals; that's what keeps the day safe and the route right.
- **Sun protection:** you're on open water the whole time. Use reef-safe sunscreen, and leave the floppy hat at the hotel; it won't survive the ride.
- **Bring** a dry bag for phones and cards, a towel and a dry T-shirt for the ride home.
- **Don't touch the coral.** Float, look and let the fish come to you.
- **Budget:** $80 per person, with transfers, the boat, the snorkel gear and the guide included.
- **Ask about driver requirements** (like minimum age) when you book.

## Ready to take the wheel?
If your idea of romance comes with a little adrenaline and a lot of salt spray, this is your day. Message us on WhatsApp with your hotel and your favorite pickup hour, and we'll save a boat for the two of you.

title: Mom, Look Down! How Parasailing Finally Impressed Our Teenagers
caption: The Millers from suburban Chicago brought two teens who are 'over' everything. Twenty-five minutes above the Punta Cana coastline changed that.
prelude: Our 15- and 17-year-old had rated every activity of the trip 'fine.' After parasailing, the word was 'insane,' and for once they meant it as a compliment.
post:
## The teenager problem
If you travel with teens, you know the look: earbuds in, eyebrows half-raised, waiting to be unimpressed. The resort pool was 'fine.' The buffet was 'fine.' We needed something with real adrenaline that was also safe enough for Mom to sign off on. Parasailing turned out to be the one thing everybody agreed on in the family group chat. Even Grandma, who wasn't coming, sent a thumbs-up.

## Short, simple, no wasted day
Round-trip hotel transportation is included, and the activity itself runs about 25 minutes. That's the beauty of it: it doesn't eat your vacation. We went in the morning and were back at the pool before the kids had finished complaining about getting up.

## The speedboat ride out
The adventure starts before you ever leave the water. A speedboat takes you out to the flight zone, bouncing across the waves while the beach shrinks behind you. Our son, who claims nothing can surprise him, held the rail with both hands and laughed the entire way.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## Safety first, then sky
Before anyone goes up, the crew walks you through the safety equipment with bilingual instruction and checks every strap and buckle. As parents, that part mattered to us more than anything else. Then comes the moment: the line lets out, the canopy fills with wind, and you rise up and away until the engine noise fades to almost nothing.

## The view everybody talks about
From up there, Punta Cana looks like a painted map. The sea is layered in every shade of blue and turquoise, the sand is a thin white ribbon, and the palm trees line the coast like a row of tiny brushstrokes. Our daughter said it was the quietest she'd felt all year. Our son yelled 'Mom, look down!' so loudly we heard him from the boat. That's the video we'll play at every holiday dinner from now on.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Tips for families with teens
- **Check the requirements first:** ask us about minimum age and weight limits when you book, so nobody gets a surprise on the boat.
- **Want to fly with your kid?** Ask at booking whether flying together is possible on your date.
- **Wear** a swimsuit or quick-dry clothes; the boat ride is splashy.
- **Strap your sunglasses** or leave them on board, and keep phones in a waterproof pouch with a lanyard.
- **Sun:** there's little shade on the boat. Reef-safe sunscreen and a rash guard go a long way.
- **Eat light** beforehand if anyone in the family gets seasick.
- **Budget:** $80 per person, with hotel transport, the boat ride, all safety gear and the flight included.

## Your family's best photo of the trip
If you're looking for the one moment that gets your teens to put the phone down, or at least point it at something amazing, this is it. Message us on WhatsApp with your hotel and everyone's ages, and we'll help you plan the flight.

title: Thirty-Five, Sequins and a Show That Never Stops: Tasha's Birthday at Coco Bongo
tour: Coco Bongo: The World's Best Party
caption: Six friends from Atlanta, one birthday girl and five hours of acrobats, tribute acts and movie-style effects. Here's how to plan the birthday night of the trip.
prelude: We'd planned the beach days down to the minute. The birthday night, we left to Coco Bongo, and it delivered more than any of us could have planned.
post:
## Why Coco Bongo for a birthday
Tasha didn't want 'just a club.' She wanted a night with a wow factor, something that felt like a celebration before the first song even ended. Coco Bongo is exactly that: more world-class spectacle than nightclub, with over 15 high-production shows every night. Acrobats overhead, tribute artists, lighting and effects straight out of a movie. You don't have to plan the entertainment; it happens all around you.

## Getting there (and back) without the stress
The night runs about five hours, and a round-trip hotel transfer comes with the admission ticket. For a group of six, that's huge: no hunting for taxis in heels, nobody stuck figuring out a ride home. Our rule was simple: we arrive as six, we leave as six.

[[IMAGE-1]]

## The show, the show, the show
From the moment the lights dropped, we barely sat down. One act would end and another would start somewhere else in the room: on stage, above the crowd, sometimes right next to us. The tribute performances had the whole place singing along, and the acrobats got gasps out of even the most jaded of us (that would be Kayla). Every few minutes someone grabbed a friend's arm: 'Look up!'

## Drinks and ticket tiers
What's in your glass depends on the ticket tier you choose, because the drink packages are tied to it. The listed price is $90 per person. If your group cares about a fuller package or a better spot, ask us to compare the options before you book, so there are no surprises on the night.

## The birthday-girl moment
Our best moment wasn't planned at all. A song came on that Tasha has loved since high school, the whole group screamed, and for three minutes we were seventeen again. That's the magic of a night like this: the show creates the moments, and all you have to do is be there with your people.

[[IMAGE-2]]

## Girls'-trip tips for a great (and safe) night
- **Use the organized transfer** both ways. It's included, and it keeps the group together.
- **Drink water** between cocktails. Caribbean heat, hours of dancing and a drink package deserve respect.
- **Keep valuables to a minimum:** a small crossbody bag, one card, your phone and a photo ID. Passports and good jewelry stay in the hotel safe.
- **Cute-but-comfy shoes.** You'll be on your feet for hours.
- **Pick a meeting spot** inside, in case anyone gets separated.
- **Eat a real dinner** before you head out.

## Make it a birthday to remember
